source_documents.title: Internal Audit Plan 2025-2028
source_documents.what_it_is: Covering report to the Governance Committee (29 April 2025) seeking approval of the 2025-2028 Internal Audit Plan, Internal Audit Charter and review of the Internal Audit Strategy. Describes the plan's standards, structure and the team, and lists Appendices A-F by name. Appendix D (the plan itself, with audit areas/risk levels/days) and all other named appendices are NOT included in this file - only the covering report text is present.

source_documents.title: Risk Management Strategy
source_documents.what_it_is: Committee report (12 December 2024) proposing a revised Risk Management Strategy, including a new 5x5 risk matrix and risk appetite. Pages 1-4 are the covering report; pages 5 onward are Appendix A, the Risk Management Strategy document itself, containing the scoring method (impact/likelihood scales, appetite, matrix, RAG bands, Corporate Risk Register inclusion rule) and a glossary of risk category examples.

gaps.item: agreed_actions (individual actions/recommendations with due dates or status)
gaps.status: Searched all three audit/plan papers (audit-completed-work-2024-25-annual.pdf, audit-completed-work-2025-26-q3.pdf, internal-audit-plan-2025-28.pdf). discrepancies.description: Para 4.3 prose mislabels the Medium rating as 'Medium (2)' - the same number already used for Minor - instead of 3. Table 1 itself (the row order and the 5x5 matrix) places Medium at score 3, between Minor (2) and Major (4).
discrepancies.quote: Negligible (1), Minor (2), Medium (2), Major (4), or Critical impact(5):

discrepancies.description: In Table 1 (Impact Ratings), the 'Personal / Staff or Customers' column is defined as death/injury/illness for the Critical, Major and Medium rows (Death; Permanent disability; Major injury/hospitalisation) but switches to financial-loss wording for the Minor and Negligible rows ('Major financial loss £1,000+ Illness e.g. stress / minor accident / RIDDOR' and 'Minor Financial loss up to £1,000 / complaint / Grievance'), inconsistent with the column header and with the higher-severity rows. This pattern is present in both the plain and the -layout extraction, so it is a feature of the source table, not an extraction artefact.
discrepancies.quote: Major financial loss £1,000+ Illness e.g. stress / minor accident / RIDDOR

discrepancies.description: Figure 1 (5x5 risk matrix, p.18) labels the cells scoring 8-12 'High', but Table 4 (RAG levels, p.19) names the band covering the same score range (8-12) 'Medium High' (Amber) - the matrix never uses the words 'Medium High' for any cell, only 'Low', 'Moderate', 'High' and 'Extreme'.

Para 6.3 frames escalation to the Corporate Risk Register in terms of risks 'considered to be extrene [sic, extreme] (Red)' on the matrix (i.e. the Extreme band, scored 15-25), but Figure 4's explicit inclusion rule for the Corporate Risk Register is 'Score 9 or above', which also captures the Medium-High/Amber band (8-12), not only Extreme/Red risks. The two statements on the same page do not describe the same threshold. Para 6.3 also contains a typo, 'extrene' for 'extreme'.

evidence.quote: Where risk levels are considered to be extrene (Red) on the risk matrix, the appropriate Service Director must escalate the risk to the Executive Director
Includes risks that: Score 9 or above

discrepancies.description: Table 1 financial percentage bands overlap: Medium is 0.1%–0.3% and Major is 0.25%–1%. The printed GBP endpoints also do not imply one consistent budget conversion. Preserve both columns as printed; do not infer or repair a budget. The assessment method must explain which descriptor it uses.
